summary: The run had a strong Act 1 foundation, including several upgrades and a successful Hexaghost fight, but Act 2 traded away too much maximum HP and deck quality for short-term sustain. The resulting 56-max-HP deck reached the Champ with little margin for error, and the final combat included inefficient energy use on an attack turn.

lessons.title: Treat the Bite transformation as a major HP-and-deck commitment
lessons.situation: When offered the event that removes Strikes for five Bites at the cost of maximum HP, especially before difficult Act 2 combats or a boss.
lessons.lesson: Accept the Bite trade only when the immediate healing and Strike removal clearly outweigh the permanent maximum-HP loss. Otherwise, preserving maximum HP and avoiding five mediocre attacks can provide more reliable survivability and scaling.
evidence_points: Act 2 Floor 19: accepted removal of all Strikes, received 5 Bites, and lost 24 max HP, changing HP from 56/56 afterward.
The final 30-card deck contains five Bites and has only 56 maximum HP.
The run later reached the Champ after repeatedly losing HP, with the final combat starting from a fragile 35/56 HP state in the combat summary.
lessons.reasoning: The event permanently reduced the run's health ceiling while adding a large package of similar cards. Although Bites supplied healing, the final deck and low maximum HP show that the trade left less room to absorb Act 2 and Champ damage.

lessons.title: At critical HP, buy immediate combat safety before optional relics
lessons.situation: When entering a shop at low HP shortly before a boss or dangerous combat and several purchases compete for limited gold.
lessons.lesson: Prioritize a potion or defensive card that improves the next fight before buying multiple long-term relics. Preserve enough gold for an immediate survival tool unless the relic is directly essential to the upcoming fight.
evidence_points: At the Act 2 Floor 29 shop, the run had only 19/56 HP and available options included Dexterity, Attack, and Cultist potions, Metallicize, and other defensive cards.
Instead, it bought card removal, Centennial Puzzle, Hand Drill, and True Grit, reducing gold from 420 to 47 before the Champ.
The final build lists no potions, and the run then proceeded through the Champ fight with very little HP margin.
lessons.reasoning: The purchases improved the long-term build but consumed nearly all resources while the immediate constraint was survival at 19 HP. A potion or stronger defensive purchase could have addressed the next combat more directly; the evidence does not prove which specific alternative was best, but it supports changing the priority order.

lessons.title: Do not spend two energy on draw after already committing to defense on an attack turn
lessons.situation: During a low-HP enemy attack turn when several defensive cards have already been played and only a small amount of energy remains.
lessons.lesson: First reach a sufficient block threshold, then use leftover energy for damage or efficient draw. Avoid adding a two-energy Burning Pact after Shrug It Off and Defend unless the additional cards are necessary for survival or provide a clearly stronger line.
evidence_points: Champ Turn 17 began at 23/56 HP with 4 energy, 0 block, and an ATTACK intent.
The sequence played Shrug It Off, then Defend, then Burning Pact, leaving 9 block and only 1 energy before discarding Doubt and playing Bite.
At the Burning Pact decision, Bite and Wild Strike were legal alternatives, while the final state still had only 9 block against the Champ's attack.
lessons.reasoning: The logged sequence spent most of the turn on defense and then used the remaining two energy on draw, producing only one attack while ending with a modest block total. Exact incoming damage is not recorded, so the counterfactual is uncertain, but the sequence demonstrates a reusable need to evaluate survival first and avoid inefficient late-turn energy spending.
